name: Ankara
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Ankara: defence supply chains, public procurement counterparties, IP disputes and Turkish company research.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Ankara, scoped from Nashville: background research on defence and engineering suppliers, counterparties in public contracts, trademark and IP disputes heard in Ankara's courts, and lawful fact-finding for counsel in Türkiye's administrative and judicial capital.
intro: Ankara is Türkiye's capital and second-largest city. TÜİK address-based registration data put the province's population at 5,864,049 on 31 December 2024. As the seat of government, the city concentrates ministries, regulators and the state institutions that award and oversee large public contracts. It is also the centre of the national defence industry: an Ankara Chamber of Industry report cited in 2025 attributes about half of national defence industry turnover in 2024 to Ankara-based firms such as ASELSAN, TUSAŞ, ROKETSAN and MKE. Ankara's exports reached about 15 billion dollars in 2024, led by weapons and ammunition, special-purpose machinery and chemicals.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Ankara because so many decisions that matter to business in Türkiye are made or contested there. Foreign manufacturers and integrators need to know who stands behind local suppliers, subcontractors and agents in defence and aerospace supply chains. Companies bidding for or performing public contracts want to understand the ownership and connections of partners and intermediaries. Brand owners litigate trademark cancellations against decisions of the Turkish Patent and Trademark Office in Ankara's specialised courts. Investors and lenders want reliable background on Ankara-based groups whose growth has depended on state customers, licences and permits.

matters.title: Defence supply chain counterparty research
matters.text: Background research on Ankara-based suppliers, subcontractors and agents in defence and aerospace programmes, covering ownership, management, related companies, litigation and media history, so that foreign primes and integrators can assess partners and meet their own compliance and export-control obligations.

matters.title: Public contract partner due diligence
matters.text: Research into joint-venture partners, consultants and intermediaries in public tenders and state-funded projects, focusing on beneficial ownership indicators, links to officials or politically exposed persons, prior disputes and adverse coverage, to support anti-corruption compliance before contracts are signed.

matters.title: Trademark and IP dispute support
matters.text: Factual research for counsel in trademark cancellation and invalidation actions before Ankara's IP courts, such as evidence of actual use or non-use of a mark, the history of the applicant, and links between a registrant and known infringers or former distributors.

matters.title: Integrity checks on state-linked groups
matters.text: Reputational and corporate background research on Ankara holding companies and contractors whose business depends on government customers, licences or permits, identifying concentration risk, political exposure, regulatory penalties and litigation that investors and lenders should understand.

matters.title: Asset and judgment enforcement research
matters.text: Lawful research supporting recovery against Ankara debtors, including trade registry history, directorships, related entities and publicly reported assets, to help counsel decide where enforcement proceedings or attachment applications in Türkiye are likely to be worthwhile.

local_context.title: Apex courts seated in Ankara
local_context.text: Ankara is the seat of Türkiye's highest courts, including the Court of Cassation (Yargıtay), the final appellate court for civil and criminal cases, the Council of State (Danıştay) for administrative matters and the Constitutional Court. Commercial disputes now follow a three-tier route introduced in July 2016, from commercial courts of first instance to regional courts of appeal and then the Court of Cassation, so much of the country's settled commercial case law is shaped in the capital.

local_context.title: Ankara Regional Court of Appeals
local_context.text: Ankara is one of the cities hosting a regional court of appeal, which reviews both law and facts and can send files back for retrial. Ankara's civil courts of intellectual and industrial property rights hear actions against decisions of the Turkish Patent and Trademark Office, with the Office joined as co-defendant, and appeals go to the Ankara Regional Court of Appeals. Many trademark disputes involving foreign brand owners therefore run through Ankara.

local_context.title: Energy Disputes Arbitration Center
local_context.text: The Energy Disputes Arbitration Center (EDAC), established within the Energy Law Research Institute but operating independently, began operating in Ankara in October 2020 and describes itself as an institution dedicated to energy sector disputes. Larger international commercial arbitrations in Türkiye are more commonly administered elsewhere, notably in Istanbul. Investigative support in arbitration is limited to factual research for counsel, presented in a form that can be tested.

local_context.title: Chambers and trade registry
local_context.text: Turkish companies are recorded by trade registry offices that operate within local chambers, under Ministry of Trade oversight. Ankara companies are registered through the Ankara Chamber of Commerce, while the Ankara Chamber of Industry represents the city's manufacturers and publishes industry data. Registry entries and the Trade Registry Gazette show incorporation, capital changes and authorised signatories, but share ledgers of joint-stock companies are not public, so ownership often needs corroboration from other sources.

local_context.title: Mandatory commercial mediation
local_context.text: Before filing suit on commercial monetary claims, a party must first apply to mediation; a lawsuit filed without it is dismissed on procedural grounds. Mediation is also mandatory for labour disputes. For counsel planning litigation against an Ankara counterparty, factual research on the opponent's position, assets and relationships is often most useful before the mediation stage, when settlement leverage is being assessed.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Ankara, TDSC first establishes what the client must decide, whether that is onboarding a defence subcontractor, partnering on a public contract, pursuing a trademark cancellation or recovering a debt, and which Turkish records bear on it. Desk research is conducted from Nashville using trade registry and gazette entries, published court decisions, industry and chamber publications and Turkish-language media. Because public sources rarely show joint-stock shareholders, findings on ownership are presented with their basis and level of confidence. Interviews, site visits and any other local enquiries are carried out by appropriately qualified Turkish professionals coordinated with the client's Turkish counsel, and personal data is handled with Türkiye's data protection law in mind.

faqs.q: Can you vet a defence subcontractor based in Ankara?
faqs.a: Yes, within lawful limits. We research the company's registry history, managers and authorised signatories, related entities, litigation, media coverage and connections to other programme participants. We do not access restricted defence or government records. Export-control classification and licensing questions belong with the client's trade compliance team and counsel; our findings support their assessment.

faqs.q: Why do so many trademark disputes in Türkiye involve Ankara courts?
faqs.a: The Turkish Patent and Trademark Office is based in Ankara, and actions challenging its Re-Examination and Evaluation Board decisions are heard by Ankara's civil IP courts, with appeals to the Ankara Regional Court of Appeals. We can help counsel gather facts on use, the history of a registrant and links to infringers.

faqs.q: Can you tell us who really owns an Ankara company?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but not always from one record. Trade registry entries show founders, capital and signatories, yet joint-stock share ledgers are not public and beneficial ownership information is not openly searchable. We combine registry history, gazette notices, related companies, media and litigation records, and state clearly where ownership is inferred rather than documented.

faqs.q: Is our dispute with an Ankara company subject to mediation first?
faqs.a: Under Turkish procedure, commercial monetary claims generally require an application to mediation before a lawsuit, and a claim filed without it is dismissed on procedural grounds. Whether that applies to your claim is a question for Turkish counsel. We can support the preparation by researching the counterparty's position and assets.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in Ankara?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is based in Nashville, Tennessee, and has no office or staff in Ankara or elsewhere in Türkiye. Engagements touching Ankara are scoped and managed from Nashville. Where local enquiries or legal advice are needed, we coordinate with appropriately qualified Turkish professionals and the client's Turkish counsel.
